findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the count divides evenly, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 gives 2 pages, and 100 members gives 3.

As a result, `showingLast` is false on the real last page and the UI shows '1/2'. Clicking next moves `offset` to `user_count` and loads an empty member list.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: Unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
findings.body:
`limit` and `offset` are taken straight from user params, with no cap and no lower bound. This endpoint is reachable by any user who can see the group, not just admins.

- A request with `limit=10000000` serializes every member of a huge automatic group such as trust_level_0. That is an easy way to load the database and app server.
- A negative `limit` or `offset` is passed to Postgres. Postgres rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET, so the request fails with a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..200) and clamp `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: Breaking change to /groups/:id/members response shape
findings.body:
The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`, and non-automatic groups are now paginated to 50 by default where previously the full list was returned.

Any other client of this endpoint will silently break or receive truncated data. That includes external API consumers, plugins, and other front-end code that calls `/groups/:name/members` and expects an array.

The change and default limit should be documented, or existing consumers audited.

findings.title: Admin create/update no longer accept nested `group[...]` params or usernames
findings.body:
`create` and `update` now read top-level `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, and so on instead of `params[:group][...]`. The `usernames` and PATCH `changes` interfaces were removed.

API clients that still send nested `group` params will create groups with an empty name, which fails validation. On update they will silently reset `visible` to false, because `params[:visible]` is nil.

This is an unannounced breaking change to the admin API.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body:
The route for `remove_member` is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, but the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs don't enforce the verb, so the spec passes without exercising the request as the client actually sends it.

Use `xhr :delete` to match the route.

findings.title: No error handling for addMembers/removeMember failures
findings.body:
`addMembers` and `removeMember` only handle success. The controller actions `addMembers` and `removeMember` never attach a rejection handler either.

If the server returns 422 (e.g. for an automatic group) or a save error, the admin gets no feedback and the promise rejection goes unhandled. In addition, the username input is never cleared after a successful add, as the TODO acknowledges, so pressing Add again re-submits the same users.
